info.title: Agent Pulse read API
info.description: Read what your organisation's agents spent, for a dashboard of your own. Every request carries a reading api key in the X-Api-Key header and names your organisation in the path; a request naming any other is refused. Nothing here writes: recording happens through the recorder library over gRPC.

400.description: The request could not be read: a missing window, one that ends before it starts, a groupBy or filter field not served, or a parameter the method has no field for.

401.description: The key is missing, unknown or revoked. These are answered identically, so probing learns nothing.

403.description: A recording key was used to read, or the request named an organisation the key does not belong to.

429.description: Over the plan's rate limit. Try again shortly.

get.summary: Lists activities under an organisation, most recent first by default.

400.description: The request could not be read: a missing window, one that ends before it starts, a groupBy or filter field not served, or a parameter the method has no field for.

401.description: The key is missing, unknown or revoked. These are answered identically, so probing learns nothing.

403.description: A recording key was used to read, or the request named an organisation the key does not belong to.

429.description: Over the plan's rate limit. Try again shortly.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description:
The organisation whose activities to list.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}`

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Maximum activities to return. Defaults to `100`, capped at `1000`.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: A page token from a previous response, to retrieve the next page.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Optional filter, confining the page to activities matching every term.

A filter is one or more terms joined by `AND`, each `field = value`,
e.g. `agent = "organisations/acme/agents/atlas" AND status = FAILED`.
A value may be quoted; it must be when it holds a space. The fields are
the ones activities can be grouped by: `agent`, `model`, `provider`,
`user`, `caller_service`, `caller_component`, `skill`, `status`,
`error_code` and `kind`. Only equality is served, and only `AND`; the
window is `start_time` and `end_time`, not a term. An unknown field or
any other operator is refused rather than ignored.

Cannot widen the organisation: scope always comes from `parent`, and a
term naming an agent outside it matches nothing.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description:
Optional sort order. The one order served is `occurred_at desc`, which
is also the default, so a page is the most recent work first.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description:
Start of the window to list, inclusive. With `end_time`, confines the
page to when the work happened; without either, every activity under
`parent` is listed.

parameters.name: endTime
parameters.description: End of the window to list, exclusive.

get.summary: Returns spend grouped by one or more dimensions.
get.description:
This is what cost dashboards read. Results are always confined to the
organisation named in `parent`; the organisation is never taken from
`filter`, so a caller cannot widen its own scope.

400.description: The request could not be read: a missing window, one that ends before it starts, a groupBy or filter field not served, or a parameter the method has no field for.

401.description: The key is missing, unknown or revoked. These are answered identically, so probing learns nothing.

403.description: A recording key was used to read, or the request named an organisation the key does not belong to.

429.description: Over the plan's rate limit. Try again shortly.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description:
The organisation whose spend to aggregate.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}`

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description:
Dimensions to group by, e.g. `["agent", "model"]`.

Valid dimensions are `agent`, `model`, `provider`, `user`,
`caller_service`, `caller_component`, `skill`, `status`, `error_code`,
`kind`, `date` and `hour`. `kind` is `model`, `tool` or `call`: a tool
call is one recorded under a `tool:` component, a model call one that
names a model or counted tokens, and a call is anything else. `date` and
`hour` are UTC. An empty list returns a single total for the whole
organisation.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Optional filter, with the same terms as [ListActivitiesRequest.filter],
so a panel asks for exactly the rows it draws: `user = "8c21e0b4"` grouped
by `date` is one person's spend by day, without the rest of the
organisation's rows being read and discarded. Cannot widen the
organisation. `agent` below is the same as a filter term on `agent`,
kept for callers that only ever confine to one.

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description: Start of the window to aggregate, inclusive.

parameters.name: endTime
parameters.description: End of the window to aggregate, exclusive.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description:
Maximum rows to return. Defaults to `100`, capped at `1000`.

Grouping by several dimensions at once can produce a great many rows, so
this method paginates like a list rather than returning everything.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: A page token from a previous response, to retrieve the next page.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description:
Optional. Confines the aggregate to one agent's activities.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}/agents/{agent}`; must sit under
`parent`.

ActivityProvider.description:
The provider that billed for a call.

 - VERTEX_AI: Google Vertex AI. The only provider whose charges can be reconciled
against a Google invoice.
 - ANTHROPIC: Anthropic, called directly rather than through Vertex AI.
 - OPENAI: OpenAI.
 - PERPLEXITY: Perplexity.

PriceableUnitKind.description:
What a rate is charged against.

 - PROMPT_TOKENS: Tokens in the prompt.
 - CANDIDATE_TOKENS: Tokens the model generated.
 - CACHED_TOKENS: Prompt tokens served from the provider's cache.
 - CACHE_WRITE_TOKENS: Prompt tokens written to the provider's cache.
 - REASONING_TOKENS: Tokens the model spent reasoning.
 - REQUEST: A whole request, e.g. one web search.

name.title:
The resource name of the activity.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}/activities/{activity}`

agent.description:
A registered resource rather than a free string, so that spend can always
be attributed to something with a known owner.
agent.title:
The agent that performed the work.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}/agents/{agent}`

request.description:
Opaque identifier of the end-user request this activity belongs to.

Every activity produced while serving one user request carries the same
value, including across a handoff from one agent to another. This is what
makes cost per unit of business work possible: outcomes attach to the
request, and the request's activities sum to its cost.

session.description:
Opaque identifier of the conversation or session, where the product has
one. Empty for work that is not conversational.

user.description:
Opaque identifier of the person the work was done for.

An identifier, never an email or a name. Recorders take it from the
verified request context rather than accepting it as an argument, so that
one person's spend cannot be attributed to another.

The name behind it, where the organisation supplies one, is held once at
`organisations/{organisation}/users/{user}` with this value as the last
segment, so it cannot contain `/`.

callerService.description: The service that made the call, e.g. `atlas-agent`, `deep-research`.

callerComponent.description:
The part of the calling service that spent the money, e.g. `chat_turn`,
`tool:web_search`, `research_merger`.

Derived by the recorder from the surrounding framework call, so adopting
teams do not set it per call site. A free string on the wire: adding a new
component never requires a contract change. Values an agent did not
declare in `Agent.components` are still accepted, and reported, so that
drift is visible rather than silent.

skill.description:
The area of the product the person was using, e.g. `canvas`,
`doc_viewer`, `social`.

Distinct from `caller_component`, which is a code path. This is a product
concept the framework cannot infer, so it is set once on the request
context by products that want to slice cost this way, and left empty
otherwise.

model.description:
The model that was called, as the provider names it,
e.g. `gemini-2.5-pro`.

provider.description: The provider that billed for the call.

cachedTokens.description:
Prompt tokens served from the provider's cache, which are usually billed
at a different rate from ordinary prompt tokens. Counted separately so the
rate card can price them correctly.

cacheWriteTokens.description:
Prompt tokens written to the provider's cache. Some providers bill a
premium for this, so it is priced separately rather than folded into
`prompt_tokens`.

reasoningTokens.description:
Tokens the model spent reasoning, where the provider reports them apart
from the visible response.

totalTokens.description:
Total tokens the provider reported for the call. Recorded as reported
rather than summed locally, so the figure can be checked against the
provider.

estimatedCostMicros.description:
What the call is expected to cost, in millionths of a US dollar.

Computed by the server from token counts, `charges` and the rate card in
force at `occurred_at`. Available immediately, and approximate. Money is
an integer count of millionths rather than a floating-point amount so that
sums are exact.

billedCostMicros.description:
What the call was actually billed, in millionths of a US dollar.

Written by the nightly reconciliation from the cloud billing export, and
zero until that has run. Only populated for charges that appear on a
Google invoice; a provider called directly is never reconciled, and this
stays zero for those. Where both figures are present, this one is the
truth and `estimated_cost_micros` is the estimate it corrected.

rateCardVersion.description:
The version of the rate card used to price this activity.

Recorded so that a later change to provider pricing does not silently
rewrite what history cost.

charges.description:
Charges not measured in tokens, such as a per-request search fee.

Repeated because one call can incur several. A token-only call has none.

durationMs.description: How long the call took, in milliseconds.

errorCode.description:
The provider or platform error code, where the call did not succeed.

A code, never a message: provider exception messages can quote the prompt.

occurredAt.description:
When the work happened, as reported by the recorder.

Preserved as supplied. The server falls back to its own clock only when
this is omitted, so that a batch delayed in transit is still priced and
reported against the time it actually occurred.

updateTime.description:
When this activity was last updated, which for most activities is when
reconciliation wrote `billed_cost_micros`.

v1Activity.description: One priced unit of agent work.

v1ActivityStatus.description:
How a call ended.

 - OK: The call completed.
 - FAILED: The call failed. Cost is still recorded, because a provider charges for
work done before a failure.
 - DENIED: The call was refused before it reached the provider, by a spend limit or
a guardrail. Usually costs nothing, but is recorded so that refusals are
countable.
 - TRUNCATED: The call was cut short, by a token limit or a deadline. Partial work was
done and is charged for.

name.title:
The resource name of the agent.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}/agents/{agent}`

product.description: The product the agent belongs to, e.g. `rezco`, `dealade`, `voyage`.

service.description:
The service the agent runs in, e.g. `atlas-agent`. Matches
`Activity.caller_service` for activities this agent produces.

owner.description:
Who to ask about this agent's spend. A team name or a role, not a person,
so it survives people changing jobs.

components.description:
The components this agent expects to report, e.g. `chat_turn`,
`tool:web_search`.

Advisory, not enforced. An activity naming a component that is not listed
here is still recorded, and is counted in a drift report, so that a team
adding a component never has a write rejected but a team whose components
have quietly diverged can be told.

updateTime.description: When this agent was last updated.

v1Agent.description: An agent whose spend is recorded.

rows.description: One row per combination of the requested dimensions.

nextPageToken.description: Token to retrieve the next page, empty when there are no more.

dimensions.description:
The dimension values for this row, keyed by dimension name, e.g.
`{"agent": "organisations/acme/agents/atlas", "model": "gemini-2.5-pro"}`.

estimatedCostMicros.description: Sum of `estimated_cost_micros` over the matching activities.

billedCostMicros.description:
Sum of `billed_cost_micros` over the matching activities. Lower than the
estimate where reconciliation has not yet run for part of the window.

totalTokens.description: Sum of `total_tokens` over the matching activities.

activityCount.description: How many activities the row covers.

promptTokens.description:
Sums of each kind of token, kept apart because each is priced at its own
rate and a total cannot be taken back apart once summed.

failedCount.description:
How many of the activities failed or were denied: neither produced the
work the call was made for.

truncatedCount.description: How many hit a limit and did partial work.

unpricedCount.description:
How many model calls used tokens and were priced at nothing, which is
what a call looks like when the rate card could not match its model.

modelCalls.description:
How many of the activities were model calls, and how many tool calls,
by the same rule as the `kind` dimension. The two do not have to sum to
`activity_count`: a call that names no model, counted no tokens and ran
no tool is neither.

A tool call carries no model, so a row grouped by `model` holds the tool
calls under an empty value rather than leaving them out.

distinctRequests.description:
How many distinct requests and people the activities belong to. Exact
for the window asked for, and not additive across windows: a person
active on two days is one person in a two-day window.

p50DurationMs.description:
Duration at the 50th and 95th percentile, in milliseconds, over the
activities that reported one. Approximate, and not additive across
windows.

firstOccurredAt.description: When the earliest and latest of the activities happened.

v1AggregateRow.description: Spend for one combination of grouping dimensions.

priceableUnit.title:
The priceable unit being charged for.
Format: `priceableUnits/{priceable_unit}`

quantity.description: How many of the unit were consumed, e.g. `3` web searches.

estimatedCostMicros.description:
What this charge is expected to cost, in millionths of a US dollar.
Computed by the server from the rate card.

v1Charge.description: A charge that is not measured in tokens.

nextPageToken.description: Token to retrieve the next page, empty when there are no more.
Token to retrieve the next page, empty when there are no more.
Token to retrieve the next page, empty when there are no more.

priceableUnits.description: The priceable units in this page.

nextPageToken.description: Token to retrieve the next page, empty when there are no more.
Token to retrieve the next page, empty when there are no more.

name.title:
The resource name of the outcome.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}/outcomes/{outcome}`

outcomeDefinition.title:
The kind of outcome being counted.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}/outcomeDefinitions/{outcome_definition}`

request.description:
The request that produced it, matching `Activity.request`.

The join between work done and money spent. A request with no outcome
recorded simply has no cost-per-outcome figure; it is not an error.

quantity.description:
How many were produced, e.g. `12` candidates on one shortlist. Zero is
meaningful: it records a request that produced nothing.

updateTime.description: When this outcome was last updated.

v1Outcome.description: A count of business outcomes produced by one request.

name.title:
The resource name of the priceable unit.
Format: `priceableUnits/{priceable_unit}`

displayName.description: Human-readable name, e.g. `Gemini 2.5 Pro output tokens`.

provider.description: The provider that charges for it.

model.description:
The model this rate applies to, where the charge is per model. Empty for a
charge that is not model-specific, such as a web search.

unitCostMicros.description:
Deprecated: too coarse to hold a real rate. Use `unit_cost_nanos`.

A single token often costs a fraction of one millionth of a dollar —
Gemini input is 1.25 millionths — so a whole number of millionths cannot
express it and rounds every such rate down. Left in place rather than
removed, and never read.

unitCostNanos.description:
Cost of one unit, in billionths of a US dollar.

Billionths rather than millionths because a per-token rate is routinely a
fraction of a millionth, and rounding one to a whole millionth undercounts
every token priced against it. An activity's cost is still stored in
millionths; the extra precision belongs to the rate, not to the money.

effectiveFrom.description: When this rate takes effect, inclusive.

effectiveTo.description: When this rate stops applying, exclusive. Empty while it is current.

rateCardVersion.description:
The rate card version this belongs to, recorded on every activity priced
with it, e.g. `2026-09`.

source.description:
Where the rate came from, e.g. a link to the provider's public price list.
Kept so a figure can be traced back to a published price.

updateTime.description: When this rate was last updated.

v1PriceableUnit.description: One line of the rate card.

name.description:
`{user}` is the identifier exactly as the organisation's agents stamp it
on `Activity.user`; that equality is the whole join. It is the bare
identifier the organisation's sign-in issued, never an email, and it
cannot contain `/`.
name.title:
The resource name of the user.
Format: `organisations/{organisation}/users/{user}`

displayName.description: The person's name as the organisation would show it, e.g. `Ada Lovelace`.

email.description: The person's email address, where the organisation chooses to send it.

createTime.description: When this user was first named.

updateTime.description: When this user was last written.

v1User.description: A person an organisation's agents do work for, named.

Error.description: How a refusal is answered. The code is the gRPC status by name; the message says what to change.

ApiKey.name: X-Api-Key
ApiKey.description: A key issued on the console's API keys page as Reads. A key issued as Records is refused here.
